json.title: ADR 0006: RPMS deployment topology — direct adapter vs customer-side connector
json.body:
## Why

Today corvid's implicit deployment model is **SaaS reaches inbound into each customer's RPMS** (VPN / proxy / private CA). That works for one customer; it scales poorly to 5–50 tribal sites with heterogeneous IHS-OIT firewall postures. The May 27 IHS correspondence (Daniel McMurtrey, Portland Area) confirms that customer-side firewall is OIT-Group-Policy-controlled, with the authoritative security spec held at the Area Office — not at the tribal site.

Before we harden pooling, retry, circuit-breaker, or model decoupling, we need a decision on the production deployment shape.

## Three modes to evaluate

- **Mode 1 — Single-tenant direct.** One corvid host, one pinned adapter. Useful today.
- **Mode 2 — Multi-tenant direct (inbound to each customer RPMS).** SaaS reaches into customer networks via VPN/proxy/private CA. Per-tenant routing. Painful at scale.
- **Mode 3 — Customer-side connector (recommended north star).** Small Lakeraven-provided binary runs inside the customer network; opens an *outbound* persistent connection (mTLS WebSocket or queue) to corvid SaaS; proxies RPMS reads/writes locally. Customer firewall only needs outbound egress.

## Decisions this ADR must settle

- Recommended deployment topology (Modes 1/2/3) and the rationale.
- For Mode 3 connector: transport (mTLS WebSocket vs queue), reconnect/backoff, message envelope.
- Where RPMS credentials live (customer-side in Mode 3; secret-manager-referenced in Mode 1/2).
- Adapter router shape — factory/config resolver, not static registry. Resolves to either a direct adapter or a connector-shaped adapter.
- Audit ownership: which side records the RPC-level audit trail vs the workflow-level decision.
- **RPMS broker session user-context** — service account vs per-end-user DUZ. This answer gates the rpms-rpc pool key shape (one global slot vs keyed on user/facility).

## Blocks

This ADR gates the following:
- AdapterRouter implementation
- rpms-rpc connection pool design (pool key needs the user-context answer)
- Operational runbook (Mode 2 vs Mode 3 docs are very different)
- Customer-side connector binary design

## Out of scope

- Implementation of any mode — this is a decision artifact only.

Recorded by ADR 0006 (#397, merged 2026-07-28): customer-side connector (Mode 3, outbound mTLS WebSocket) is the north star; Mode 1 direct kept for pilots/dev; Mode 2 inbound not built. All six decisions settled, incl. the `(tenant, facility)` rpms-rpc pool key with a named per-user-DUZ revisit trigger. Contingent premise (PRC-data PHI content in legacy RPMS) tracked in #409 — refines emphasis, not the decision. Unblocks #390, #391, #392, and the rpms-rpc pool design.
